name: DevSeek programming-agent target benchmark
goal: Expose whether DevSeek behaves like a coding agent comparable to Claude Code/Codex, not merely whether the provider pipe returns text.

cases.description: CLI can run one prompt and emit machine-readable AgentEvent JSONL.
cases.expectedCapability: The agent has a reliable noninteractive protocol for automation.

cases.description: Given a model create_file tool call, DevSeek must create the requested file in the workspace and the generated program must compile and run.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent applies structured file edits instead of only printing them.

cases.description: Given an existing program and a replace_file tool call, DevSeek must update the file, preserve old behavior, add new behavior, and pass the verifier.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent modifies existing projects safely rather than only generating new text.

cases.description: When the first generated edit fails verification, DevSeek must feed the failure back to the model, apply the repair, and rerun the verifier.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent closes the loop around failing tests.

cases.description: A coding run that changes files must emit file change, validation, and quality-gate events in JSONL.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent leaves auditable evidence for automation and review.

cases.description: Given a unified diff for an existing file, DevSeek must apply the patch, preserve old behavior, add new behavior, and pass the verifier.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent can apply reviewable patches, not only full-file replacement tool calls.

cases.description: Given a small Node project with an npm test script, DevSeek must apply the edit and run the project verifier rather than only relying on file syntax.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent discovers and runs project-specific validation commands.

cases.description: Across two CLI turns in one workspace, DevSeek must create code, then handle a new user requirement by passing the existing source file as context, preserving old behavior, and verifying the new behavior.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent carries workspace context into follow-up requirements instead of asking the model to guess existing code.

cases.description: Given an interactive C++ CLI and a devseek verifier config, DevSeek must compile it, execute it with stdin, assert expected stdout, and include that evidence in validation events.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent can validate programs that require user input, not only noninteractive binaries.

cases.description: Given a multi-file C++ project and a devseek verifier config, DevSeek must create all files, compile linked translation units, run the binary, and preserve command evidence.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent can validate realistic multi-file programs instead of compiling only one file at a time.

cases.description: Given a Python implementation and devseek verifier config, DevSeek must run Python-based verification with stdout assertions.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent supports common language runtimes beyond C++ and Node when tests are explicitly configured.

cases.description: Given a follow-up coding request that does not name exact files, DevSeek must still attach small relevant project files as model context and validate the change.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent can orient itself in a small workspace without requiring the user to list every file path.

cases.description: Given a model file tool call that attempts to write outside the workspace, DevSeek must refuse the edit and leave parent paths untouched.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent enforces workspace boundaries while applying autonomous edits.

cases.description: Given a formal UAV main-control maintenance request with requirement docs, platform interface docs, main-control anchors, reference communication code, requested design docs, target-module implementation, and self-loop tests, DevSeek must attach those context files, create an integration design with source fact matrix, concrete protocol constants, remote-controller interface schema, and existing-code modification plan, implement inside zc_maintenance, run the verifier, and avoid standalone demo code.
cases.expectedCapability: A coding agent can handle existing formal-project work as a software-engineering workflow: source-fact discovery, architecture-aware interface design, target-module implementation, and automated validation evidence.

failurePolicy: A passing provider pipe is not enough; missing file edits, missing verification, or missing repair loops are product gaps.
If all cases pass without exercising a real file mutation and verifier, the benchmark is invalid.
Every failure must be classified as DevSeek capability gap, test design gap, or environment gap, then recorded under docs/testing/programming-agent-benchmark-reports.
